brief: Distinguish a credit report’s recorded information from a score derived from it.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Record and score"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Historial y puntaje"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Histórico e pontuação"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Distinguish a credit report’s recorded information from a score derived from it.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: A number cannot show you which account contains a mistake.
instruction.misconception: A credit score and the underlying account records are interchangeable.
instruction.numeracy_support: Every quantity and assumption needed to decide is visible in the current scenario. Examples explain the relationship before independent application.

evidence.reasoning: A report lists account history. A score summarizes risk using a model; inspect the report to check specific entries.
The report contains the entry you need to inspect.
The model summarizes information rather than listing each account.
The number alone does not identify a changed record.
Records and a calculated summary serve different purposes.
Different models can summarize the same information differently.
The report lets you inspect the unfamiliar account itself.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Retrieve this competence in the declared later course reviews and through the existing shared review system.
